thought.label: How the seed was applied
thought.contrastBody: Label on fill and fill on canvas, both themes, against WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and SC 1.4.11.

alert.title: Check

unreadable.title: The token stylesheet could not be read
unreadable.description: This page derives a brand from the canvas colours and ramp steps the document is painting, read from the live stylesheet. Neither could be read here, so nothing below it would be a measurement.

order.title: Seed, then role, then scope, then instance
order.description: Stop at the first level that does the job. Every level below the seed is a value that has stopped deriving, and nothing tells you when the brand moves past it.

seed.title: 1. Seed
seed.description: The brand's action colour: what a primary button is filled with. In most cases this is the whole theme.
seed.label: Brand seed
seed.helper: A six digit hex. Everything below derives from it and is measured against WCAG 2.2 AA.
seed.presetHelper: Each of these produces an answer a well behaved blue hides.

preset.very-light: Near white: the fill cannot clear the light canvas
preset.very-dark: Near black: the dark seed runs to white
preset.sunflower: Sunflower: repoints the state steps in both themes

announce.one: Seed {hex}. Light {light}, dark {dark}. {pass} of {count} measured pair clears AA.
announce.other: Seed {hex}. Light {light}, dark {dark}. {pass} of {count} measured pairs clear AA.

seed.announceNoDark: Seed {hex}. No lightness at this hue and saturation carries a readable fill on the dark canvas, so there is no dark theme to measure.

derived.title: 2. What the seed produces
derived.description: Read only, because these are results. Three roles per theme are written into the export; the rest derive from the primary in scope at the element that paints them, so writing them would pin them to this seed.

contrast.title: 3. Contrast
contrast.description: Every pair the seed produces, measured with the package's own WCAG helper. A label on its fill owes 4.5:1 (SC 1.4.3); a fill on the canvas behind it owes 3:1 (SC 1.4.11).

overrides.title: 4. Per token overrides
overrides.description: Below the seed on purpose. Reach for one only when the seed is right and a single token must differ.
overrides.costDescription: A token set by hand stops following the seed. The next brand change moves everything derived and leaves this value behind, and no audit reports it.
overrides.labelHelper: By default the label is chosen by the seed's own luminance, the same 0.179 threshold a runtime re-theme uses. Forcing it is the one override the generator has a flag for.
overrides.darkHelper: Contrast parity with the light theme puts it at {parity}. Hue and saturation are held either way; only lightness moves. An authored value is allowed to fail, and the table above is how it says so.
overrides.darkNoParity: No lightness at this hue and saturation clears both floors, so there is no parity value to depart from.

export.title: 5. Export
export.description: Paste the first block into your own theme file and the second over the baked email palette, which no stylesheet can reach.
export.divergesWhy: The dark seed's lightness was authored here. The generator searches for parity and has no flag for it, so no command reproduces this file.
export.noDarkTitle: This seed has no readable dark fill
export.noDarkDescription: No lightness at this hue and saturation clears both 4.5:1 on its own label and 3:1 on the dark canvas. Desaturate the seed, or force the label above and look again.

## First week

Read your team's **release procedure** and finish [[Setup|environment setup]] before joining your first review.

pageReader.lead: What a new member does in their first week. Work through it from the top.
pageReader.s1p1: IT issues your account. When you first sign in to the internal portal, set up two-factor authentication.
pageReader.s1p2: Collect your laptop at the general affairs desk. Check the asset number and sign the receipt when you collect it.
pageReader.s2p1: Install the dependencies by following the repository README. If a step fails, share the full error in your team's channel.
pageReader.s2p2: Once the app runs locally, sign in with a test account and go through the main screens once.
pageReader.s3p1: Read your team's release procedure and look through about three past release notes.
pageReader.s3p2: At the end of the week, hold a 30-minute retrospective with your mentor. Writing down what was unclear beforehand helps.

chartsDocs.areaSplitTitle: AreaChart · fill apart from stroke / cropped value axis
chartsDocs.areaSplitBody: series[].fillColor sets the band's colour independently of the line's color, and valueDomain / valueTicks state the value axis outright. A non-zero baseline is legitimate only where the SHAPE is the message and zero is not a meaningful reference — a price, a temperature, an index, a latency percentile. In any figure that asks the reader to compare magnitudes (every bar chart), it exaggerates the wobble and misleads. If you crop, say the range and keep the grid.

page.subtitle: A themed region whose overlays keep the region's tokens.
page.title: ThemeScope

intro.title: Why a region needs this at all
intro.description: Every overlay portals to document.body, so custom-property inheritance stops at the portal boundary.
intro.body: A region that themes itself themes its own subtree and nothing it opens: measured on a scoped theme, the region read --primary 204 100% 37% and the Dialog it opened read 268.7 100% 50%, the package default. ThemeScope carries the computed difference between the region and the document root to a host at the portal destination, so the overlay inherits it by containment. It has no theme prop — it reads the DOM, which is why an inline style, a class and a stylesheet rule all behave the same.

longList.title: Long child lists (height · virtual · filterTreeNode)
longList.description: 2 suites → 28 sections → up to 421 cases. With height the tree scrolls inside that height and renders only the rows in view (antd height + virtual). Nodes matching the search are highlighted by filterTreeNode, never hidden. Section 2 fails its first loadData and fetches again when reopened. Section 3 shows how to compose a paged API: selecting the last leaf loads the next 100.

drag.title: Drag to reorder or reparent (draggable · allowDrop · onDrop)
drag.description: Drop on the upper quarter of a row to land before it, the lower quarter after it, the middle inside it. Tree never edits treeData; onDrop reports the move. From the keyboard: Alt+↑ / Alt+↓ move past a sibling, Alt+← outdents, Alt+→ indents into the previous sibling. Every move is announced in a live region. Here allowDrop refuses dropping inside “Release notes”.
drag.keys: When draggable: past a sibling / outdent / indent

breadcrumbExamples.parentsDescription: currentItem="none" keeps every ancestor linked without marking a current page. PageContainer uses breadcrumbCurrentItem="none" when the record name is its title. Ellipsis preserves the full accessible name and title, with no repeated tooltip description.
breadcrumbExamples.ellipsisTitle: ellipsis · a long segment on one line
breadcrumbExamples.ellipsisDescription: ellipsis on a segment keeps the trail on one line and cuts that label with "…"; the full label shows in a tooltip on hover and when the crumb link takes keyboard focus. antd Breadcrumb has no per-item ellipsis — the shape is Typography’s. PageContainer breadcrumb takes the same item field.

avatarDocs.fitDescription: cover (the default) crops to fill — right for a face. contain shows a wide or transparent logo whole.
avatarDocs.agentDescription: Where an agent could be mistaken for a person — a member list, an assignee, a comment author — its mark carries an "AI" tag. The tag sits on the top corner, so it composes with the presence dot at the bottom. Screen readers hear "AI agent", so colour is never the only signal.
avatarDocs.agentListTitle: A list that shows names: the mark AND the label
avatarDocs.agentListDescription: Where the name is printed — a member list, a people picker, a comment author — use Avatar kind="agent" and put <AgentBadge /> right after the name.

rangeTimelineDocs.resizeTitle: Resizable label column, loading, undated rows
rangeTimelineDocs.resizeDescription: Drag the divider in the header (or focus it and use the arrow keys, Shift for bigger steps, Home/End) to widen the label column. The width is controlled, so an app can remember it per user. The switch marks a range as loading; a row without dates shows a hint instead of a bar.
rangeTimelineDocs.longTask: EXSELI-81 Rebuild the contact form and its confirmation email
rangeTimelineDocs.schedulesDescription: A phase heading row with no hint, bars against a baseline (overrun and early labels), a milestone diamond with its hollow baseline, an open-ended row with no end grip, a cancelled row, a finish recorded without a start, and dependency arrows: a violated one gets a focusable marker. Emphasis marks the critical path and an at-risk row.

page.subtitle: Submit-driven search for lists: a 検索条件 form, a condition builder, an advanced-search form and a list view with a docked filter panel.
page.decision: Which shape: a few filters applied as the user changes them → FilterBar. Many conditions, a heavy query, or users who expect an explicit Search button → SearchForm (l). Power users combining any field with any operator and saving the result as a view → a condition builder (m, o). A one-off expert query with syntax help → an advanced-search form (n).

topbarIdentityDocs.title: Shared-device identity
topbarIdentityDocs.name: Demo Barista
topbarIdentityDocs.description: The signed-in name stays visible. Topbar identity reserves at most 40% of the bar; TopbarItem truncate ellipsises only the name and keeps the full name in its title and accessible text.
topbarIdentityDocs.policy: Primary controls keep their minimum sizes. At extreme widths the other clusters follow scroll, clip or menu; identity stays outside. Use TopbarSearch for search. Do not combine identity with labelHideBelow, hideBelow or iconHideFrom. Theme knobs: --topbar-identity-max-inline-size and --topbar-identity-min-text-inline-size.
